cards.method: Classical univariate forecasting: ARIMA, ETS, Theta and TBATS
cards.when: univariate forecasting of one ts with automatic ARIMA/ETS, a robust Theta baseline, or TBATS for multiple/non-integer seasonalities

alternatives.criterion: you want a keyed indexed-table workflow, distribution-valued forecasts, or several models fitted at once
you need ETS+ARIMA+regression unified or a non-gaussian error
holidays/calendar effects dominate

output_key_fields: mean: point forecasts (ts -> {values,start,frequency})
lower/upper: prediction interval bounds per level (matrix)
level: confidence levels (80,95)
fitted/residuals: in-sample one-step values for diagnostics
accuracy: training-set measures (RMSE,MAE,MAPE,MASE,ACF1)
model: fitted object (compact stub in to_mcp)
interpretation_traps: accuracy(fc) is in-sample (training-set), NOT out-of-sample generalisation — for OOS use 15-model-evaluation (tsCV/DM) or a holdout
MAPE is unstable/infinite when y≈0 (growth rates) — prefer MASE (<1 = better than naive)
ETS/ARIMA prediction intervals assume gaussian innovations — they understate under heavy tails
run_auto_arima gate: exog_handle not a data frame + NROW(exog_handle)==length(y); run_tbats gate: NCOL(y)==1
y must be a series with the correct frequency, otherwise a non-seasonal fit results
sources: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos FPP3 (ARIMA/ETS)
Hyndman & Khandakar 2008 JSS 27(3) (automatic ARIMA order selection)
Assimakopoulos & Nikolopoulos 2000 (Theta); Hyndman & Billah 2003 (Theta=SES+drift)
De Livera, Hyndman & Snyder 2011 JASA (TBATS)
Hyndman, Koehler, Ord & Snyder 2008 (ETS state-space)
forecast reference manual

cards.method: Tidy ARIMA and ETS forecasting over grouped series
cards.when: ARIMA/ETS over many keyed series at once (an indexed table + a model formula) with distribution-valued forecasts, manual pdq/PDQ orders, or the ETS state components
cards.when_not: a single plain series without the keyed-table overhead (-> #7); Theta/TBATS/multiple seasonality (-> #7); non-gaussian (-> #10); intermittent demand (-> #135)

alternatives.criterion: non-long-format quick use or Theta/TBATS
ETS+ARIMA+exog_handle together or a different error distribution

output_key_fields: forecast: a table carrying a distribution column -> quantile grid (probs+mean+sd); median≈point
glance: 1-row sigma2/log_lik/AIC/AICc/BIC + ar_roots/ma_roots (complex -> {re,im})
long-format: coefficients (term,estimate,std_error,statistic,p_value)
components: ETS-only dable with states (level,slope,season)
fitted/residuals: in-sample (type innovation vs regression)
interpretation_traps: <distribution> is NOT a number — take median or mean, not the raw cell
ar_roots/ma_roots are complex; stationarity/invertibility ⇒ modulus>1 (sqrt(re^2+im^2))
glance does NOT compute accuracy — for OOS you need new_data + accuracy (15-model-evaluation)
missing values: ETS is a hard error (the gate rejects any gap), ARIMA reverts with a warning — do not confuse the two
sources: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd ed.
Hyndman, Koehler, Ord & Snyder 2008, Forecasting with Exponential Smoothing: the State Space Approach

cards.method: Additive/logistic-trend forecasting with holidays and multiple seasonalities (Prophet)
cards.when: decomposable additive trend+seasonality(Fourier)+holidays+regressors with automatic changepoints; calendar effects, gaps/irregular index, an interpretable decomposition
cards.when_not: clean monthly/quarterly macro series without a calendar (ARIMA/ETS are more accurate); autoregressive dynamics; a very short series

alternatives.criterion: clean low-frequency macro series without calendar structure
explanatory regressors with state-space rigour
the objective is causal impact, not a forecast

output_key_fields: forecast: df records; ds,yhat(point),yhat_lower/upper(interval),trend,*_terms(components)
future: the future df (ds + regressors)
regressor_coefficients: center/coef per regressor (only with regressors)
cv: per cutoff yhat,y(actual),cutoff,ds,horizon (run_prophet_cv)
metrics: horizon + mse/rmse/mae/mape/mdape/smape/coverage
interpretation_traps: the default interval_width=0.8 ⇒ 80% intervals, NOT 95%
without mcmc_samples>0 the intervals capture trend uncertainty only (MAP) — they understate
run_prophet_cv is expensive (many re-fits)
horizon/units in cross_validation are time units (180 days ≠ 180 monthly periods)
coverage in metrics must be ≈ interval_width for calibrated intervals
gates: seasonality_mode∈{additive,multiplicative}; logistic->cap; regressors->an explicit future with the columns; macro spacing>=28d auto-disables weekly/daily
sources: Taylor & Letham 2018 Forecasting at scale (The American Statistician)
prophet reference manual + Facebook Prophet docs

cards.when: ADAM unifies ETS+ARIMA+regression in state space with a non-gaussian error (dlaplace/ds/dgamma/..) or intermittent demand (occurrence); CES when trend/season are hard to separate
cards.when_not: a plain gaussian monthly series (-> #7, ETS/automatic ARIMA suffices); holidays (-> #9); distribution-valued forecasts over keyed series (-> #8)

alternatives.criterion: the classic gaussian path, lighter
long-format workflow
calendar effects

output_key_fields: mean: point forecasts (conditional mean, ts)
lower/upper: bounds of interval=prediction at level=0.95 (side both)
level/interval: the level + a binary flag for whether an interval was produced
accuracy: automatic holdout (MASE/RMSSE) when holdout=True, otherwise in-sample
model: adam/ces object (states,persistence,phi,complex params) compact stub
fitted/residuals: in-sample
interpretation_traps: fit-time level=0.99 is the outlier-detection level, NOT forecast confidence (that is interval_level 0.95)
h/holdout are fit-time; the forecast horizon is the separate forecast_h (explicit->fit h if >0->10)
accuracy is holdout (OOS) only if holdout=True, otherwise in-sample
in run_auto_adam the distribution and in run_auto_ces the seasonality are lists of candidates to be tried, not a single enumerated choice
gate: holdout=True requires h>0 (in all 4)
sources: Svetunkov 2023 Forecasting and Analytics with the ADAM (openforecast.org monograph)
Svetunkov & Kourentzes (CES / complex exponential smoothing)

cards.method: Neural-network univariate forecasting: MLP ensemble and extreme learning machine
cards.when: non-linear univariate forecasting; nn_mlp=an MLP ensemble (backprop), nn_elm=an Extreme Learning Machine (random hidden weights, output lasso/ridge/step/lm); automatic lag selection + differencing + seasonal dummies; an ensemble of reps networks
cards.when_not: a small sample/interpretability/a linear DGP -> #7 forecast or #10 smooth; multivariate -> 03-multivariate-nowcasting; without a seed it is uncacheable (forbidden)

alternatives.criterion: the linear/interpretable path with analytic PI (lightweight)
state-space ETS+ARIMA (non-gaussian/intermittent)
speed (closed-form output weights, no backprop) rather than full MLP training

output_key_fields: mean: point forecasts (the ensemble combination via comb, ts)
all_mean: h x reps — ALL the ensemble members
lower/upper: EMPIRICAL PI (per-horizon quantiles of the members; NOT analytic; it needs reps>1)
accuracy: the in-sample ME/RMSE/MAE/MAPE, computed here because the network forecast does not report them
model: the mlp/elm object -> producer register field=model bucket=rds; a compact stub in to_mcp
hd/lags/difforder/reps/seed/n: the selections + the pinned seed (cache key)
interpretation_traps: the seed is MANDATORY & part of the cache key — the same seed gives identical output, a different one a different forecast (live-verified)
the PI are empirical ensemble quantiles, NOT frequentist/Bayesian intervals
exog_handle must cover in-sample + horizon (length >= n+h)
the defaults reps=2/hd=3 are curated to be cheap (the docs use reps=20); raise them deliberately
gate: y must be ts/msts (a plain vector is rejected); hd/reps positive integers; level in (0,100); exog_handle not a data_frame
sources: Ord, Fildes & Kourentzes 2017 Principles of Business Forecasting 2e Ch.10
Kourentzes, Barrow & Crone 2014 neural network ensemble operators (Expert Systems with Applications 41(9))
Huang, Zhou & Ding 2006 Extreme Learning Machine (Neurocomputing 70(1))

cards.method: Recursive autoregressive machine-learning forecasting with conformal prediction intervals
cards.when: univariate forecasting with an ML learner on lagged+fourier features (recursive AR); rml_fit=ARml+forecast (point+PI), rml_conformal=distribution-free conformal PI, rml_variable_importance=variable importance; a CLOSED whitelist of light learners (least squares, elastic net, ridge, lasso)
cards.when_not: a full neural network -> #133; a linear, interpretable model with analytic intervals -> #7; state-space ETS and ARIMA -> #10; multivariate -> category 03; a free choice of learner is NOT allowed (security and cost); without a seed the node is uncacheable

alternatives.criterion: a full/ELM NN for non-linearities rather than regularized ML
the linear/interpretable path with analytic PI (lightweight)
you need explicitly distribution-free (residual-based) PI rather than the parametric ones of rml_fit

output_key_fields: mean: point forecasts (ts, recursive AR)
lower/upper: the h x length(level) PI of forecast.ARml (conformal-calibrated)
accuracy: in-sample ME/RMSE/MAE/MAPE (computed here from residuals/fitted)
model: the ARml object -> producer register field=model bucket=rds; a compact stub in to_mcp
learner_method/max_lag/seed/n: the public learner token + the pinned values (cache key)
rml_conformal: the lower/upper conformal bounds + confidence + n_calibration; rml_variable_importance: an importance df (variable/overall)
interpretation_traps: the seed is MANDATORY and part of the cache key — the same seed gives identical output (live-verified); the resampling is stochastic
the public learner token is mapped INTERNALLY (ridge and lasso become an elastic net at a fixed alpha); it is NOT a free-form string
an exog_handle at fit time requires a future newxreg (nrow==h) for the forecast
conformal PI are distribution-free (residual-based), NOT gaussian; rml_conformal is a separate tool
gate: y must be a univariate series longer than max_lag+1; cv=False is rejected; the learner is a closed whitelist; level in (0,100); confidence in (0,1)
sources: Vovk, Gammerman & Shafer 2005, Algorithmic Learning in a Random World (conformal prediction)
Bostrom 2022 crepes: a Python Package for Generating Conformal Regressors (PMLR 179)
Hyndman & Athanasopoulos Forecasting: Principles and Practice 3e (fourier/recursive forecasting)

cards.method: Intermittent / sparse-demand forecasting (Croston + SBA/SBJ variants, TSB, iMAPA auto-selection, Croston decomposition)
cards.when: demand series with many zeros (spare parts / rare events); a constant out-of-sample demand rate; automatic model selection (imapa) or a demand/interval decomposition
cards.when_not: a dense series with no zeros -> #7; charts (the frontend; plotting is off); continuous macro series

alternatives.criterion: bias-corrected Croston (SBA/SBJ) — less positive bias
declining demand / obsolescence (it models the demand probability, not the interval)
automatic robust model selection (a combination across aggregation levels)
the series is NOT intermittent (it is dense)

output_key_fields: forecast: the out-of-sample demand RATE (length h; a constant per-period rate, NOT discrete events)
fitted: the in-sample demand rate (with leading blanks); weights/initial: the smoothing and initialisation parameters; model: the selected model
the iMAPA summary: a matrix per aggregation level (level/n/p/cv2/model — 1=Croston, 2=SBA, 3=SES — and whether it was used); model_fit: the parameters per level
the Croston components: the in-sample and out-of-sample demand and interval, plus the SBA/SBJ scaling coefficient; decomp: demand + interval, of equal length
interpretation_traps: forecast = a demand RATE per period (e.g. 0.19 units/period), NOT a forecast of an individual order — sum it for total demand
tsi_croston does NOT validate the type -> silently wrong; negative values are silently accepted -> a non-negativity gate; h<=0 gives a silently empty forecast
intermittency gate: >=1 zero (otherwise it is dense -> #7) AND >=2 non-zero values; imapa ALs with use=0 (<4 obs) are ignored; deterministic (no seed)
sources: Kourentzes 2014, On intermittent demand model optimisation and selection, IJPE 156:180-190 (doi:10.1016/j.ijpe.2014.06.007)
Petropoulos & Kourentzes 2015, Forecast Combinations for Intermittent Demand, JORS (doi:10.1057/jors.2014.62)

cards.method: Long memory / fractional integration ARFIMA(p,d,q) (ML fit + GPH/Sperio semiparametric d + fractional differencing)
cards.when: a slowly decaying ACF, between I(0) and I(1); estimating the memory parameter d (semiparametric GPH/Sperio or parametric ARFIMA ML) + fractional differencing to I(0)
cards.when_not: integer differencing -> ADF/KPSS plus differencing, category 01; a forecast object -> #7-#10; long-memory volatility -> GARCH, category 06

alternatives.criterion: a fast semiparametric estimate of d (GPH log-periodogram) — the exploration default
a more robust semiparametric d (smoothed periodogram, Parzen window) under short-run dynamics/noise
a full parametric ARFIMA(p,d,q) ML (d+AR/MA+SE together) when you need a model, not just d

output_key_fields: d + d_reading: d≈0 short memory (I0), d<0 anti-persistent, 0<d<0.5 stationary long memory, d>=0.5 non-stationary
arfima_gph/arfima_sperio: sd_asymptotic/sd_regression (two SE estimators for d -> a CI/significance of d!=0)
arfima_fit: d/ar/ma/sigma/log_likelihood/std_errors(order d,ar,ma)/covariance/correlation + model (a producer, rds)
arfima_difference: series (fractionally differenced; it preserves the ts attributes) + d + n
interpretation_traps: the arfima_fit drange default c(0,0.5) CONSTRAINS d to [0,0.5] — for d>=0.5 (non-stationary) widen drange explicitly
MA sign: this estimator uses the convention with REVERSED MA signs relative to the usual ARIMA parameterisation — do not compare the coefficients directly
BANDWIDTH GATE: arfima_gph and arfima_sperio with a zero bandwidth exponent return a blank d and an infinite standard error SILENTLY (silently wrong) -> a hard gate, 0 < bandwidth < 1
the covariance and standard errors of the ML fit can be inaccurate (a documented warning) — prefer the semiparametric standard error for inference on d
sources: Haslett & Raftery 1989 (Applied Statistics 38:1-50, ML approximation)
Geweke & Porter-Hudak 1983 (J. Time Series Analysis 4(4):221-238, GPH)
Reisen 1994 (J. Time Series Analysis 15(1):335-350, smoothed periodogram)
Jensen & Nielsen 2014 (J. Time Series Analysis 35(5):428-436, fast fractional difference, doi:10.1111/jtsa.12074)
precondition_tools: the series precheck (a univariate numeric series with no gaps, NaN or infinities)
c00_data_utilities/descriptive_statistics.desc_acf (a slowly/linearly decaying ACF => evidence of long memory)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_suite.unitroot_adf (ADF non-rejection + ambiguous stationarity => possible fractional integration)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_suite.unitroot_kpss (KPSS alongside ADF for an ambiguous I(0)/I(1))
c00_data_utilities/replacement_missing_values.impute_kalman (fill the gaps before the fit, if needed)

cards.method: Distributed-lag & ARDL regression (finite DL / Koyck geometric / autoregressive DL / Almon polynomial DL)
cards.when: a lag-distributed effect of a predictor X on Y (short/long-run multipliers): a finite q, an infinite geometric decay (Koyck), an autoregressive DL(p,q), Almon polynomial smoothing of the lag weights
cards.when_not: pure univariate forecasting without X -> #7/#8; non-linear relations; I(1) long-run cointegration/ECM -> ARDL bounds (05); structural shocks/IRF -> 04

alternatives.criterion: x,y are I(1): a bounds test for long-run cointegration + an ECM instead of a level DL regression
an infinite geometric decay of the lag weights (a single rate phi, parsimony) rather than an explicit finite q
many lags with multicollinearity -> Almon polynomial smoothing of the lag weights
you need AR dynamics in Y (autoregressive) alongside the distributed lags of X

output_key_fields: coefficients: named numeric (intercept + lag terms); fitted/residuals: numeric
diagnostics: r_squared/adj_r_squared/sigma/df_residual/nobs/aic/bic (aic and bic are blank for the Koyck IV fit)
method-specific: q/k (finite/poly); order=c(p,q) (ardl); geometric_coefficients alpha/beta/phi (koyck); beta+beta_tvalue/beta_pvalue (poly); formula/removed (multi-formula mode)
interpretation_traps: Koyck: interpret the geometric_coefficients (alpha/beta/phi, with phi the decay rate), NOT the raw IV delta coefficients; aic and bic are blank because the IV fit has no log-likelihood — do not compare it with least-squares models
poly: beta (the original per-lag weights) is the interpretable quantity; the coefficients are the gamma of the z-transformed polynomial, NOT per-lag effects
q loses q initial observations (nobs = n - q); a length mismatch between x and y would be accepted SILENTLY -> a hard gate
closed formula: it is built from y_col ~ x_cols (reformulate), NEVER a free formula string; k>q -> singular (hard gate)
sources: Hill, Griffiths & Judge, Undergraduate Econometrics (Wiley); Baltagi, Econometrics 5th ed. (Springer)
precondition_tools: c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (stationarity of x & y first — a level DL regression on non-cointegrated I(1) series is spurious)

cards.method: Maximum Entropy Bootstrap for time series (dependence/non-stationarity preserved)
cards.when: bootstrap ensemble replicates of a series for downstream inference/confidence bands WITHOUT assuming stationarity or tuning a block length (it preserves dependence/non-stationarity)
cards.when_not: parametric prediction intervals from a correctly specified model -> forecast #7; charts (frontend); panel pdata_frame ensembles (out of scope)

alternatives.criterion: a well-specified parametric model exists -> model-based prediction intervals instead of resampling
preserve the CLT for the ensemble mean; False for non-gaussian tails, or for a trim with an xmin=0 non-negativity constraint

output_key_fields: ensemble: an n x reps matrix of replicates (nested rows) — the data and producer field
x: the original series (as input); xx: the ordered order statistics; z: the class-interval limits
xmin/xmax: the left/right tail limits; dvtrim: the trimmed mean deviations; kappa: the scale adjustment
n/reps/trim/seed: metadata + the applied arguments (the seed for reproducibility)
interpretation_traps: STOCHASTIC: the seed is MANDATORY (the generator is seeded before the draw); without a pinned seed the node is uncacheable
reps<10, or a trim outside [0,0.5), would be accepted SILENTLY -> hard gates here (silently wrong)
force_clt=True alters the ensemble so that its mean satisfies the CLT — it is NOT a raw resample
the elapsed-time report is forced off and omitted — it is non-deterministic and breaks caching
sources: Vinod, H.D. (2006) Maximum Entropy Ensembles for Time Series Inference in Economics, J. Asian Economics 17(6):955-978
Vinod, H.D. (2013) Maximum Entropy Bootstrap Algorithm Enhancements, SSRN 2285041
Vinod & López-de-Lacalle 2009 JSS 29(5) (maximum entropy bootstrap for time series)

cards.method: Benchmark forecasters: naive, seasonal naive, drift, mean and window average
cards.when: every skill-based accuracy metric and every 'does the model beat a random walk' claim needs these as the denominator
cards.when_not: you already have a benchmark and only need the sophisticated model

alternatives.criterion: the series is seasonal
the series trends and a random walk with drift is the honest baseline
the series is noisy and mean reverting

output_key_fields: forecast: the benchmark path
intervals: prediction intervals, which for a naive forecast widen with the square root of the horizon
method: which benchmark produced it
residuals: in-sample errors, the scale MASE is computed against
interpretation_traps: a model that fails to beat SEASONAL NAIVE on seasonal data has no value, however sophisticated it looks
naive prediction intervals assume independent errors; with autocorrelated residuals they are far too narrow
MASE is scaled by the in-sample naive error, so a benchmark computed on a different sample makes the metric incomparable
sources: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos 2021, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd ed., ch.5
Hyndman & Koehler 2006 (International Journal of Forecasting 22:679-688)
statsforecast

cards.method: Dynamic regression and regARIMA with exogenous regressors
cards.when: the series is driven by observable exogenous variables and the residual dynamics still need an ARIMA structure
cards.when_not: the exogenous variables are not available over the forecast horizon; the relationship is a cointegrating one and belongs in an error-correction model

alternatives.criterion: no useful exogenous information
regressors plus autocorrelated errors
the regressor's effect is distributed over time

output_key_fields: params: regression coefficients and ARIMA parameters
forecast: conditional on supplied future regressors
residual_diagnostics: whiteness of what remains after both parts
aic, bic
interpretation_traps: forecasting requires FUTURE VALUES of every regressor; using actuals produces an in-sample illusion, and forecasting the regressors adds their error to yours
regressors and ARIMA errors compete to explain the same variation; the coefficient changes materially with the error specification
differencing applies to the regressors too, and applying it to only one side breaks the relationship
sources: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos 2021, ch.10
Box, Jenkins, Reinsel & Ljung 2015, Time Series Analysis, 5th ed.
statsmodels

cards.when: measuring the effect of a dated event -- a policy change, a strike, a methodology break -- on the level or dynamics of a series
cards.when_not: the event date is unknown (-> break tests); there are so many interventions that the model is unidentified

alternatives.criterion: a permanent level shift
a one-off effect
the effect builds and decays over several periods

output_key_fields: effect: the estimated intervention effect and its shape over time
params: intervention and ARIMA parameters together
counterfactual: the path implied without the intervention
significance: test of a zero effect
interpretation_traps: the intervention SHAPE -- step, pulse, gradual -- is imposed, not estimated; the wrong shape can make a real effect insignificant
an intervention at the very end of the sample is barely identified because there is almost no post-event data
pre-intervention model misspecification loads onto the intervention estimate, which is why the pre-period fit must be checked first
sources: Box & Tiao 1975 (JASA 70:70-79)
Enders 2015, Applied Econometric Time Series, 4th ed., ch.5
statsmodels

cards.method: Simulation-based fan charts and scenario paths
cards.when: communicating forecast uncertainty as a distribution of paths rather than a point, and imposing scenarios on that distribution
cards.when_not: the model's analytic intervals are adequate and the extra simulation adds nothing

alternatives.criterion: the model has closed-form intervals and errors are Gaussian
the model is nonlinear or errors are non-Gaussian
you want paths consistent with a stated future

output_key_fields: fan: quantile bands per horizon
paths: the simulated trajectories
scenario_paths: paths conditioned on a stated future
n_simulations: draws behind the bands
interpretation_traps: a fan of quantiles taken HORIZON BY HORIZON is not a set of plausible paths -- no single trajectory follows the median band, and reading it as one is a standard error
bootstrapped innovations preserve non-normality but assume the residuals are independent
conditioning on a scenario changes the distribution of everything else in the model; ignoring that gives paths that are internally inconsistent
sources: Britton, Fisher & Whitley 1998 (Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin 38:30-37)
Hyndman & Athanasopoulos 2021, ch.5
statsforecast

cards.method: Global pooled tree forecasting with lag features
cards.when: many related series, where one model fitted across all of them beats a separate model per series -- the standard modern approach for large forecast portfolios
cards.when_not: you have one series, where a global model has nothing to pool; the series are unrelated and pooling imposes false commonality

alternatives.criterion: few series, each with long history
many short related series
very many series and nonlinear cross-series structure

output_key_fields: forecast: paths per series
feature_importance: which lags and features drive the model
cv_score: cross-validated accuracy over the horizon
n_series: how many series were pooled
interpretation_traps: tree models CANNOT EXTRAPOLATE beyond the range of the training target; a trending series must be differenced or detrended first or forecasts flatten
feature construction must respect the forecast origin -- a lag shorter than the horizon is unavailable at prediction time and leaks
pooling assumes the series share dynamics; scale differences must be handled or large series dominate the fit
sources: Januschowski et al. 2020 (International Journal of Forecasting 36:167-177)
Makridakis, Spiliotis & Assimakopoulos 2020 (International Journal of Forecasting 36:54)
mlforecast

cards.method: Bagged and bootstrap-aggregated forecasts with STL and block bootstrap
cards.when: reducing forecast variance by averaging over bootstrap replicates of the series, which usually beats the single fitted model
cards.when_not: the series is short, where the bootstrap replicates are nearly identical and bagging adds cost without benefit

alternatives.criterion: the model is stable and the series is long
the model is unstable or the series is short
you have several different models rather than replicates

output_key_fields: forecast: the bagged mean or median path
replicate_forecasts: the individual paths, which give an empirical interval
n_replicates: how many were generated
variance_reduction: spread of replicates against the single fit
interpretation_traps: bagging reduces VARIANCE, not bias; a systematically wrong model bagged many times is still systematically wrong
the bootstrap must preserve serial dependence -- an iid bootstrap of the series destroys exactly what is being forecast
the spread of replicate forecasts is not a prediction interval; it omits innovation uncertainty entirely
sources: Bergmeir, Hyndman & Benitez 2016 (International Journal of Forecasting 32:303-312)
Petropoulos, Hyndman & Bergmeir 2018 (European Journal of Operational Research 268:545)
statsforecast

cards.when: forecasting each horizon with its own model trained directly on that horizon's target, avoiding the error accumulation of recursive iteration
cards.when_not: the horizon is one; the sample is too short to train a separate model per horizon

alternatives.criterion: one model iterated forward, efficient but accumulates error
one model per horizon, no accumulation but more models
you want a compromise

output_key_fields: forecast: the path assembled from per-horizon models
models: one fitted model per horizon
horizon_scores: accuracy per horizon, which reveals where the strategy pays
strategy: which reduction was used
interpretation_traps: DIRECT and RECURSIVE forecasts differ systematically: recursive accumulates model error, direct loses efficiency by fitting each horizon separately -- neither dominates
the direct strategy fits a different model per horizon, so the resulting path can be non-smooth or even non-monotone in ways a single model would not produce
each horizon's training set is shorter than the last, so late horizons are fitted on less data
sources: Ben Taieb, Bontempi, Atiya & Sorjamaa 2012 (Expert Systems with Applications 39:7067-7083)
Chevillon 2007 (Journal of Economic Surveys 21:746)
sktime

cards.when: prediction intervals with a finite-sample coverage guarantee that does not depend on the model being correctly specified
cards.when_not: the residuals are not exchangeable in a way any conformal variant can handle; you need a full predictive density rather than an interval

alternatives.criterion: the model is correct and you want efficiency
you want a guarantee and have data to spare
the error distribution shifts over time

output_key_fields: intervals: lower and upper bounds per horizon
coverage_guarantee: the nominal level the construction guarantees
empirical_coverage: realised coverage on the calibration set
width: interval width, the price of the guarantee
interpretation_traps: standard conformal guarantees rest on EXCHANGEABILITY, which time series violate; the time-series variants weaken this and their guarantee is correspondingly weaker
the guarantee is MARGINAL over the calibration distribution -- it does not hold conditionally on a particular covariate value or regime
a wide conformal interval is the method telling you the model is poor, not a defect of the method
sources: Vovk, Gammerman & Shafer 2005, Algorithmic Learning in a Random World
Stankeviciute, Alaa & van der Schaar 2021, Conformal time-series forecasting (NeurIPS 34)
Gibbs & Candes 2021 (NeurIPS 34)
mapie

cards.method: Automatic family selection and forecaster multiplexing
cards.when: choosing among forecasting families by a stated cross-validated rule instead of by habit, over many series at once
cards.when_not: theory or convention fixes the model; the series is too short for time-series cross-validation to leave usable folds

alternatives.criterion: within one family, cheap
across families, honest but expensive
you would rather average than select

output_key_fields: selected: the chosen model per series
cv_scores: cross-validated accuracy per candidate
selection_stability: how often the choice changes across folds
forecast: the path from the selected model
interpretation_traps: selecting on the SAME data used to report accuracy overstates performance; the selection must sit inside the evaluation loop, not outside it
a selection that flips between families across folds is telling you the candidates are indistinguishable -- combination is usually better than picking
cross-validation folds must respect time order; a random split leaks the future into the past
sources: Hyndman & Khandakar 2008 (Journal of Statistical Software 27:1-22)
Bergmeir & Benitez 2012 (Information Sciences 191:192-213)
